thread:
alex: Heads-up — I merged the helm values MR and ran `terraform plan` for staging. Plan hangs on 'Refreshing state' then fails with `Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException`. Anyone seen this after a helm/values merge?
jordan: Which backend are you using (s3+dynamodb)? Can you paste the tail of the plan output? Usually ConditionalCheckFailed => dynamodb lock cruft.
alex: Yes: backend is s3://redwood-staging-tf-state + dynamodb table tf-locks-staging. Snippet: ```Refreshing state... Error: Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed```
sam: If it's ConditionalCheckFailed it's often a competing locker. Check the lock item: `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-locks-staging --key '{"LockID":{"S":"default"}}'` and look at the `Operation` / `Who` / `expires` fields.
maria: I merged the helm values too — I bumped the k8s provider in the MR to 2.9 which might change diffing for secrets. @rachel did you kick a staging apply earlier?
rachel: Yeah I started a staging apply to smoke test the helm change but aborted it when the helm rollout got stuck. I didn't realize the pipeline would hold the dynamodb lock the whole time. Sorry.
jordan: If the pipeline still holds it and the apply is active, don't force-delete. Check the lock's `timestamp`/`expiration` and only delete if it's stale. Example safe-ish delete (replace with exact keys): ```aws dynamodb delete-item --table-name tf-locks-staging --key '{"LockID":{"S":"default"}}' --condition-expression 'attribute_exists(LockID) AND expiration < :now' --expression-attribute-values '{":now":{"N":"<epoch_now>"}}'```
alex: I tried `terraform refresh -lock=false` — it still stalls but now on k8s provider calls for `kubernetes_secret.*`. Looks like diff wants to replace secrets because the helm values changed shape.
sam: That aligns. Provider version bumps + changed `data` shape cause replaces. To mitigate: run targeted refresh/plans: `terraform refresh -target=module.db -lock=false` then `terraform plan -target=module.k8s` to see exactly what will change for the k8s secrets.
maria: Also confirm the provider version pinned in the `providers.tf` in staging. Unpinned provider upgrades are a frequent surprise.
infra-bot: Reminder: staging apply in CI started by rachel@pipelines ~10m ago — runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/terraform-locks :warning:
jordan: If you need help coordinating a safe unlock, tag me and I'll coordinate with whoever owns the pipeline. We can also snapshot the state file before any manual delete: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-staging-tf-state/staging.tfstate ./staging.tfstate.bak`.
alex: Lock item shows holder `ci-pipeline` (rachel) updated 9m ago. TTL/expiry field is set to +30s. Waiting for TTL to expire before touching.
rachel: If the lock is mine and the pipeline is hung I can finish/abort the run and release. I'll finish the aborted job in ~5m.
alex: Plan resumed shortly after TTL expiry. It now warns that `kubernetes_secret.my-secret` will be replaced. I'm going to `terraform state show kubernetes_secret.my-secret` and diff against the helm-generated secret to confirm whether it's safe to replace.
jordan: Good. If it's sensitive, consider `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [data] }` on the secret or import the new helm-managed secret into TF state manually instead of replace. Also open a tiny PR to pin the k8s provider to prevent divergent diffs.
maria: Note for postmortem: helm values changes should be paired with a terraform plan that targets k8s resources to preview secret churn.
alex: Will do the `state show` + small plan and post results here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
